title: Isomorphic Strings
statement: Two strings are isomorphic when the characters in `s` can be replaced to obtain `t`, with a one-to-one mapping. Every occurrence of a character must map to the same character, and no two characters share an image.
hints: A single map from s to t is not enough. Two source characters could collide on one target character.
Keep a map in each direction, or map both strings onto the first index where each character appeared.
The pattern of first-seen indices must be identical.

approaches.name: Two hash maps
approaches.explanation: Reject a conflicting forward or backward mapping.

approaches.name: Index signature
approaches.explanation: Replace each character by the index of its first occurrence.

editorial: Walk both strings together. If s[i] already maps to something other than t[i], or t[i] already maps to something other than s[i], the mapping is not a bijection. Otherwise record both directions. Equal strings are isomorphic under the identity map.
